question: Why is that supreme heart-mark described as dark and bearing the form of darkness?
premises: It devours the rays of māyā that produce difference.
By doing so it functions as the dissolver of all.
Dissolution of all differentiated light is represented as darkness.
inference: Because it absorbs all differentiating māyā and dissolves all, the supreme heart-mark appears dark, bearing the form of darkness.
plain_english: And because it devours the rays of māyā that produce difference, that, as the dissolver of all, is dark and bears the form of darkness.
